## Purpose

This SOP describes the field operation of the Hach DR900 portable
colorimeter for on-site water quality analysis [@hach_dr900;
@hach_water_analysis2024]. The DR900 enables rapid, field-based
measurement of nutrients, metals, and other parameters using Hach
pre-packaged reagent kits. Field colorimetry provides same-day results
when samples cannot be transported to the lab within required hold
times and supports real-time decisions during stormwater events, spill
response, or reconnaissance sampling [@apha2012].

This SOP focuses on field-specific procedures (transport, outdoor
operation, field QC). For detailed method chemistry, reagent handling,
the Method Registry, and laboratory use of the DR3900 and DR900, see
[SOP-L303 Hach Colorimetric Analysis](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field use of the Hach DR900 portable colorimeter at
  EA Program field sites for grab-sample analysis of nutrients
  (PO~4~, NO~3~, NH~3~), metals (Fe, Mn, Cu), and general chemistry
  (hardness, chloride, silica, chlorine)
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory bench-top analysis (see
  [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)); field
  turbidity (see [SOP-F205](SOP-F205-handheld-turbidity-meter.qmd));
  in situ sonde measurements (see
  [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water, groundwater, and
  stormwater field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Select analytes and approve field methods               |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the DR900 per this SOP; record results          |
| New Students      | Complete training on both this SOP and SOP-L303 before
                      independent field use                                |


## Definitions

- **Beer-Lambert law:** The linear relationship between the absorbance
  of a solution and the concentration of the absorbing analyte,
  expressed as $A = \varepsilon c l$, where $\varepsilon$ is the molar
  absorptivity, $c$ is concentration, and $l$ is path length; the
  physical basis of colorimetric analysis [@apha2012].
- **Blank (reagent blank / DI blank):** A deionized water sample
  carried through the complete analytical procedure; used to zero the
  instrument and establish the baseline absorbance of the reagent
  system; must read at or near zero before sample measurements begin.
- **Detection limit (MDL):** The minimum concentration reliably
  distinguishable from the blank; Hach method-specific MDLs are listed
  in the Method Registry in
  [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)
  [@hach_water_analysis2024].
- **Field duplicate:** A second independent measurement of the same
  sample, prepared through the full analytical procedure, to assess
  precision; RPD must be < 20% for concentrations above 5 times the
  detection limit.
- **Reaction time:** The incubation period specified in the Hach method
  protocol after reagent addition during which the color-forming
  reaction proceeds to completion; reading before reaction time has
  elapsed gives systematically low results [@hach_dr900].
- **RPD (relative percent difference):** |A - B| / ((A + B) / 2) × 100;
  used to assess duplicate precision.
- **Stored program:** A factory-programmed method on the DR900 that
  specifies wavelength, calibration curve, and units for a specific
  Hach reagent kit; accessed by program number on the instrument
  [@hach_dr900].
- **Zeroing:** The process of inserting a DI water blank into the DR900
  sample chamber and pressing Zero to set the baseline absorbance to
  zero for the selected program; required before reading samples.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hach reagent powder pillows and liquid reagents may
  contain acids, oxidizers, or heavy metal indicators. Review the SDS
  for each kit before field use. Cadmium-containing reagents (older
  NitraVer 5 formulation) are hazardous waste.
- **Physical:** Glass sample vials can break during transport; pack in
  padded cases.
- **Biological:** Water samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (required for all reagent handling)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots

### Emergency Procedures

For reagent splashes to skin or eyes, flush with clean water for at
least 15 minutes. Carry a squeeze bottle of DI water for emergency
rinsing. Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Hach DR900 Portable Colorimeter       | Charge before field day [@hach_dr900]    |
| Sample vials (10 mL, 25 mL, 1-inch round) | Matched to the methods being run     |
| Hach reagent kits                     | Check expiration dates; select analytes per project |
| DI water (squeeze bottle, ≥ 500 mL)  | For blanks, rinsing, and dilutions       |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)            | For cleaning vial exteriors              |
| Silicone oil and applicator cloth     | For 1-inch round vials                   |
| Timer                                 | Phone timer or stopwatch for reaction times |
| Waste container (sealable)            | For used reagent vials and waste solution |
| Padded carrying case                  | For protecting vials during transport    |
| Field notebook                        | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |


## Procedure

### Pre-Field Preparation

1. Identify the analytes to be measured; pack the corresponding reagent
   kits and verify none are expired.
2. Pack at least 500 mL DI water and two extra clean sample vials per
   method.
3. Charge the DR900 battery and confirm stored programs for your
   methods are accessible [@hach_dr900].
4. Print or photograph method procedure cards for each analyte (from
   the kit box or [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)
   Method Registry).

### Field Setup

1. Place the DR900 on a flat, stable surface **out of direct sunlight**.
   Direct sunlight on the sample chamber causes erroneous readings.
2. If no shade is available, shade the instrument with a jacket or
   tarp during each reading.
3. Turn on the DR900 and allow it to complete its self-check.
4. Select the stored program for your analyte.

### Blank and Calibration Check

1. Fill a clean sample vial with DI water to the fill line.
2. Wipe the vial exterior with a lint-free cloth.
3. Insert the vial, close the lid, and press **Zero**.
4. The display should read 0.00 (within the method detection limit);
   if not, clean the vial and re-zero.
5. If a known mid-range standard is available, read it immediately
   after zeroing; the result must be within ±10% of the stated value.
   Record the result in the field notebook [@hach_water_analysis2024].

### Sample Analysis

Follow the method-specific procedure from the reagent kit or
[SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) Method Registry:

1. Collect a grab sample per
   [SOP-F300](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd).
2. Fill the sample vial to the fill line with sample.
3. Add the reagent per method instructions.
4. Cap, invert, and mix as directed. Start the timer for the required
   reaction time.
5. When the reaction time is complete, wipe the vial exterior (apply
   silicone oil for round vials).
6. Insert the vial into the DR900, close the lid (shield from
   sunlight), and press **Read**.
7. Record the result, analyte, Hach method number, sample ID, units,
   date, and time in the field notebook.
8. Rinse the vial three times with DI water before the next sample.

### Waste Management

1. Collect all used reagent packets, vials, and waste solution in a
   sealable container.
2. Do not discard reagent waste in the field.
3. Return waste to the lab and dispose of per
   [SOP-L003](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Zero the instrument with DI water before each batch of samples.
- Run one DI blank and one mid-range standard at the start of each
  field session; record results in the field notebook
  [@hach_water_analysis2024].
- Analyze one field duplicate per 10 samples (minimum one per event);
  RPD must be < 20% for concentrations above 5 × the detection limit.
- If the field blank reads above the MDL, investigate contamination
  (dirty vials, contaminated DI water) and re-run.
- Note ambient temperature; some Hach methods are temperature-sensitive.
  If the sample is outside the method-specified range (typically
  20--25 °C), note the potential bias [@hach_dr900].

## Training Record

Before using the DR900 in the field independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate a complete field analysis (zero, standard check, sample
   analysis, waste collection) under supervision
3. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
